subject: EdgeCatalyst adaptor: compatibility covenant and migration plan
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@edgecatalyst.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@edgecatalyst.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T09:12:00Z
Subject: EdgeCatalyst integration — observed breaking diffs in /v2/generate

Hi Priyom,

Quick note from our devs after upgrading to your runtime image 2.3.0: several of our adaptor integration tests started failing. Specifically, the JSON structure for streaming finalization changed (v2.2 used "partial_token": true on intermediate frames; v2.3 omits that field and relies on a new "phase" enum). The change is fine from your end, but it broke our state machine in the adaptor.

I attached a short delta report (edgecatalyst_delta_report.pdf) with failing request/response examples. We have two asks:

1) Can Redwood provide a short-term compatibility toggle (server-side or header flag) that re-enables the v2.2 streaming payload shape for a 6–8 week window? That would let our customers upgrade without breaking production.

2) We want to align on a migration covenant — a clear deprecation timeline, recommended shim approach for our SDK, and a rollout gating plan so we can coordinate canaries.

We'd like to set a 30–45 minute sync this week to go over a mutual action plan. Our timeline is tight: we need either the toggle or a published shim recipe by 2026-12-22 to avoid two-week regression windows for customers.

Thanks — happy to share screen and walk through the failing traces.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Director, Integrations
EdgeCatalyst

Attachments: edgecatalyst_delta_report.pdf
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@edgecatalyst.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@edgecatalyst.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-12T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: EdgeCatalyst integration — observed breaking diffs in /v2/generate

Thanks for the detailed report, Samantha — and for the failing examples. I've looped in Vanessa (platform releases) and Marcus (SDK tools) so we can respond on both runtime and SDK sides.

Short answers up front:
- We can gate the v2.3 streaming shape behind a feature flag at the router layer and expose a header (x-rw-compat: v2.2-streaming) while we coordinate. That would be possible to enable per-customer or per-route.
- We agree a written migration covenant will help. We'll draft a short change proposal that includes: shim recipe, suggested server header, rollout gates, and a 6-week sunset window.

Action items I own for the next 48 hours:
1) Draft and share the Redwood change proposal (initial doc attached: redwood_change_proposal.md).
2) Stand up a short-lived per-route flag and test enabling it for a single EdgeCatalyst test route.
3) Schedule the sync — I'm available 2026-12-13 between 14:00–17:00 ET.

Could you confirm the timeframe that works for you and whether you prefer a Zoom or Google Meet? I'll include a short agenda: goals, toggle mechanics, shim options, canary plan, and next steps/owners.

Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha@edgecatalyst.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-13T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: EdgeCatalyst integration — observed breaking diffs in /v2/generate

+1 on the feature-flag approach; two implementation notes from Platform/Release: 

- If we expose x-rw-compat, the flag should be sticky at the route/customer level (not per-connection) so cacheing and prefix/KV assumptions remain valid.
- Suggest we include traffic-splitting support (10/90 canary) and a clear metric set (error-rate, median latency, token-dup count) to gate rollback. I've attached a short canary playbook we often use (canary_plan.xlsx).

Also: for Dedicated customers we need an explicit SLA exception path if we toggle behavior; Marcus, can your SDK team supply a minimal shim (Node + Python) that transforms v2.2 frames to v2.3-style events? If so, we can publish it as an interim compatibility package.

On 2026-12-12, Priyom Das wrote:
> Short answers up front:
> - We can gate the v2.3 streaming shape behind a feature flag at the router layer and expose a header (x-rw-compat: v2.2-streaming) while we coordinate....

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@edgecatalyst.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@edgecatalyst.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-13T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: EdgeCatalyst integration — observed breaking diffs in /v2/generate

Thanks — this looks promising. Per our internal prioritization, EdgeCatalyst can support a two-track approach:

Track A (short-term, high-priority, target by 2026-12-22):
- Redwood enables x-rw-compat: v2.2-streaming as a per-route flag.
- EdgeCatalyst will point our production test route to the compatibility flag and run a 72-hour soak; if green, we flip customer traffic.
- EdgeCatalyst engineers will also integrate the shim if you can provide one — we prefer an official Redwood-supported shim to reduce the risk.

Track B (medium-term, target by 2027-01-31):
- Joint SDK migration: EdgeCatalyst will adopt the new phase-based streaming model. Redwood will publish a migration guide and a compatibility library (Node/Python) that maps old frames to the new enum and handles edge cases.

Attached is a one-page mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan.csv) with owners and dates. Our availability for the sync: 2026-12-13 16:00–17:00 ET or 2026-12-14 09:30–11:00 ET. We prefer Google Meet.

Samantha Lee

EdgeCatalyst
